description: Add a dependency-graph view to the Epic detail page: extend the epic linked-issue read model with prerequisite edges (server), then build a client-side DAG visualization (widget) and wire it into the page with a list⇄graph toggle and graceful degradation.

tasks.title: Server: extend epic linked-issue read model with prerequisite edges and external summaries
tasks.description: Extend `LinkedIssueDto` with `PrerequisiteNumbers` (and external-prerequisite summaries) and populate them in `EpicQuerier.GetLinkedIssuesAsync` from the already-loaded `IssueInfo` data, resolving prerequisites that fall outside epic membership into `IssuePrerequisiteRefDto` ghost-node summaries. The change is additive: `EpicProgress.Build`, `nextIssue`, active/blocked sets, and `readyToMarkDone` outputs must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: `LinkedIssueDto` (packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Epic/Services/EpicDtos.cs) carries each linked issue's `PrerequisiteNumbers` and a representation of external prerequisites sufficient to render a ghost node (at minimum number, title, and status/delivery state), reusing the existing `IssuePrerequisiteRefDto` shape.

`EpicQuerier.GetLinkedIssuesAsync` populates `PrerequisiteNumbers` from `issue.PrerequisiteNumbers` and resolves external (non-epic-member) prerequisites into summaries by reusing the `IssueQuerier` dictionary already built for members (no per-issue fetch).
A linked issue whose prerequisite has no resolvable row degrades to a minimal ref so the client can render an `#N (unresolved)` ghost node rather than throwing.

`EpicProgress.Build` outputs (`deliveredCount`, `totalIssueCount`, active/blocked sets, `nextIssue`, `nextIssueReason`, `readyToMarkDone`) are unchanged by the new fields — verified by extending `EpicProgressBuildSpecs.cs` / `EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs` with cases that supply prerequisite data and assert progress outputs match the pre-change values.

Server specs assert the new fields are present on the epic detail payload (extend `EpicApiSpecs.cs` / `EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs` LinkedIssueDto mirror) and that external prerequisites are summarized with number+title+status.
`npm test` (dotnet build Mohist.sln with TreatWarningsAsErrors + Xunit) passes, including new and existing epic specs.
tasks.output: Extended LinkedIssueDto + GetLinkedIssuesAsync mapping + server specs; green `npm test`.
tasks.notes: Decision 1 & 2 from design.md. The prerequisite data is already loaded by `_issuesQuery.ListAsync` and currently dropped in the mapping — this is a mapping change, not a new data path. Default-optional DTO fields (e.g. `int[] PrerequisiteNumbers = []`) match the existing `CanStart = false` pattern so serialized-record test mirrors update mechanically.

tasks.title: Web: dependency-graph widget slice (deps, LinkedIssue type, graph model, React Flow UI, cycle guard)
tasks.description: Add the `widgets/epic-dependency-graph` FSD slice: install `@xyflow/react` + `dagre`, extend the web `LinkedIssue` entity type (and epic query passthrough) to consume `prerequisiteNumbers`/`canStart`/`startBlocker`, and implement the graph — a pure model deriving nodes (status-colored + 4-state readiness marker, waiting shows #N), directed prerequisite edges, dagre auto-layout, external-prerequisite ghost nodes, and a DFS cycle guard; plus the React Flow canvas + node components (click navigates to the issue) with no edit/start affordances. The widget is lazy-loaded so the default list view stays light.
acceptanceCriteria: `@xyflow/react` and `dagre` are added to packages/web; `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.

The `LinkedIssue` entity type (packages/web/src/entities/epic/model/types.ts) is extended with `prerequisiteNumbers`, `canStart`, and `startBlocker`; the epic query passes these through from the server DTO; existing `LinkedIssueRow` rendering is unaffected (additive fields).

A pure derivation maps `{ status, canStart, startBlocker }` to exactly one readiness state (`can-start | waiting | in-progress | done`); a `waiting` node exposes the blocking issue number (`#N`) from `startBlocker.issue.number`; node color derives from `status` (`backlog | in_progress | done | cancelled`). Unit tests cover all four readiness states and each status color.

Directed edges render from each prerequisite to its dependent (prerequisite → dependent), derived from `prerequisiteNumbers`; an edge unit test asserts direction for A→B where B declares A as prerequisite.

External prerequisites (prerequisite number not in epic membership) render as visually distinct ghost nodes carrying number+title+status; an unresolved external prereq renders as an `#N (unresolved)` ghost. Unit/component tests cover both internal (normal node) and external (ghost) cases.

A DFS cycle check runs over the edge set before layout; a cyclic fixture triggers the fallback signal (widget reports not-renderable) instead of handing a cyclic graph to dagre. Unit test covers the cyclic case.

Activating a node navigates to that issue's route; the graph renders no add/edit/reorder/delete controls and no start-issue control on nodes (read-only projection). Component test asserts navigation on click and absence of edit/start controls.
`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes with new widget model + component tests.
The widget is exported for lazy loading (`React.lazy`) so it is not bundled into the default list view.
tasks.output: `widgets/epic-dependency-graph` slice (model + UI + tests), extended LinkedIssue type + query passthrough, new deps in packages/web; green web typecheck + tests.
tasks.notes: Decisions 3, 4, 5, 6 from design.md. Covers epic-dependency-graph spec requirements: Issue Nodes Colored by Status with Readiness Markers; Directed Prerequisite Edges with Client-Side Layout; External Prerequisites Are Visually Distinct; Cycle Detection Falls Back to the List; Node Click Navigates to the Issue; Dependency Graph Is a Read-Only Projection. FSD placement follows the widgets/kanban-board precedent. Use React Flow smoothstep edges + fixed-width nodes + dagre defaults (layout tuning is a non-goal).

tasks.title: Web: epic detail page list⇄graph view toggle with small-epic and cycle degradation
tasks.description: Wire the dependency-graph widget into `EpicDetailPage`: add a segmented list⇄graph toggle in the Linked Issues Card header (local component state, not persisted), mount the lazy widget only when `linkedIssues.length >= 2`, and fall back to the list when the widget reports a cycle (or when the graph is not selected). The existing Linked Issues list view and all add/remove behavior remain intact.
acceptanceCriteria: The Epic detail page Linked Issues Card header offers a control to switch between the list view and the dependency graph view; switching does not modify epic or issue data. Component test asserts both views are reachable and data is untouched.
When the epic has 0 or 1 linked issues, the graph is not rendered and the list view is shown (toggle may hide/disable the graph option). Component tests cover the 0-issue and 1-issue cases.
When the graph is selected but the widget reports a cycle (defensive fallback), the page presents the list view instead of a broken layout. Component test covers the cycle-fallback path.

The existing Linked Issues list — including add-issue selector, remove button, and error surfaces — remains fully functional when the graph view is introduced (regression coverage in EpicDetailPage.test.tsx).
The graph widget is loaded via `React.lazy`/Suspense so the default list view does not pull in the graph bundle.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass.
tasks.output: Updated EpicDetailPage.tsx (toggle + degradation gating + lazy widget mount) + extended EpicDetailPage.test.tsx; green web typecheck + tests.
tasks.notes: Decisions 6 & 7 from design.md. Covers epic-dependency-graph spec requirements: Dependency Graph View Toggle on the Epic Detail Page; Graph Degrades to List for Small Epics (0-1 issues). The cycle-fallback scenario from Cycle Detection Falls Back to the List is asserted here at the page level (widget-level DFS guard is in T-002). Toggle state is local only — persistence is a non-goal.
